overview: Black plays 2...f5 against 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3, challenging the e4 pawn at once. White usually takes with 3.exf5, and Black has given a pawn for development and the open centre. It is a surprise weapon in the style of the Latvian and is considered unsound.

white_ideas.idea: Take on f5 and consolidate with d4 or Nc3
Return the pawn if needed to stay safe

black_ideas.idea: Open lines with ...Nf6 and ...d5 for development

typical_structures.structure: Asymmetric Sicilian structure with Black f-pawn gone

character.notes: Black risks a pawn to open the game, with the Black king also exposed.

gambit.notes: After 3.exf5 White keeps the extra pawn and Black has no forced recovery.

structure.notes: The Sicilian c-pawn trade gives an asymmetric half-open structure.

level.notes: A narrow line that is unsound.

character.reason: Black plays a risky pawn offer with forcing tactics around the centre.

gambit.reason: Black gives the f-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: It is considered unsound against sensible play.

structure.reason: It is a Sicilian-type asymmetric structure with half-open files.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never a beginner choice.

plans.reason: Black plays for activity in return for the pawn.
